Alex —

Quick heads up: I accepted the invite but my calendar is showing the slot as 6:30 PM on Thursday (local CET), which would be much later than 9:30 AM PT. My colleagues in Dublin and London see different times too — some see 17:30, some 18:30.

I attached a screenshot from my Google Calendar showing the discrepancy. Looks like when the invite was forwarded through BrightLeaf's scheduling address the TZ block dropped and Google treated it as a "floating" time for some recipients. Can you resend with an explicit timezone block (VTIMEZONE) in the ICS or just add the local time in the event title (e.g., "9:30 AM PT / 5:30 PM GMT") so attendees aren't confused?

Attachment: tz-screenshot.png (image/png)

Thanks — I'll hold the slot tentatively but want to make sure we don't have 50% no-shows because EU folks think it's evening.

Jonas Weber

Alex —

Thanks for the invite. Quick note from the SE side: forwarding an .ics from some scheduling systems strips the VTIMEZONE section or converts DTSTART to a floating time (i.e., no timezone). When that happens, Google and Outlook fall back to the recipient's default zone and interpretations vary.

Could you:
- Recreate the event from your calendar client and invite jonas.weber@redwood.com and marissa.cole@redwood.com directly (avoid passing through sched+bl), OR
- Attach the same invite but as a calendar link (Google/Exchange link) rather than a forwarded .ics, OR
- As a quick workaround, append the UTC time in the subject: "Nov 25 — 9:30 AM PT / 5:30 PM GMT / 17:30 UTC"

If you want, Ben (SE) and I can repro the exact behavior and send you a corrected .ics that includes a VTIMEZONE block targeted to Europe so all our attendees see the intended time.

Ben — can you and I generate the fixed invite and send it back to Alex to distribute? I'll create an .ics with explicit VTIMEZONE entries for PT and CET so forwarded copies will keep the TZ offsets intact.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
